query: What protocol amendment threshold and changelog format will trigger public notification of major methodological shifts to stakeholders?

response.query: What protocol amendment threshold and changelog format will trigger public notification of major methodological shifts to stakeholders?
response.answer: Major methodological shifts trigger public notification via protocol amendment thresholds and a changelog format detailing significant updates. Stakeholders receive notifications when substantial changes are outlined in the changelog.

In the ANPRM, BIS sought public comment to inform a rulemaking that would address the undue or unacceptable risks, as identified in Executive Order (E.O.) 13873, “Securing the Information and Communications Technology and Services Supply Chain,” [84 FR 22689](https://www.federalregister.gov/citation/84-FR-22689) (May 17, 2019), posed by a class of transactions that involve ICTS designed, developed, manufactured, or supplied by persons owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction or direction of a foreign adversary and integral to connected vehicles. BIS received 101 comments on the NPRM.[[1](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/16/2025-00592/securing-the-information-and-communications-technology-and-services-supply-chain-connected-vehicles#footnote-1-p5363)]  Many commenters agreed with BIS's risk assessment of foreign adversary connected vehicle technology as described in Section IV of the NPRM and supported the decision to address these risks through supply chain regulation.
